key_insight: Choose each Toffoli decomposition by both hardware error budget and circuit-specific verification, because context-dependent substitutions are only safe when their equivalence is certified in that instance.
engineering_relevance: This enables compilers to reduce costly two-qubit gates and estimated infidelity on near-term quantum hardware without silently introducing incorrect rewrites.
method: Per-Toffoli compiler pass selects among exact, relative-phase, and approximate CCX decompositions.
Accepts a context-dependent rewrite only after an instance-specific equivalence check proves validity in that circuit context.
Optimizes for two-qubit infidelity rather than raw gate count, using verification to guard every substitution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 39.5% fewer two-qubit gates and 36.7% lower infidelity on a compute/uncompute-heavy suite, 15.6% aggregate reduction on a larger benchmark set, and zero errors when the verification gate is used.
watch_item: The benefit is workload-dependent and context checks add compilation overhead, so aggressive substitutions cannot be applied safely without per-instance verification.
paper_title: Context-Verified, Error-Budget-Aware Decomposition Selection for Toffoli Networks
